rationale: Contract-stability lens. The public surface bead 2 consumes is fundamentally sound: deviation A's map-returning, seam-parameterized WithPhaseWriteLock is not merely acceptable but REQUIRED (the plan.md:531 tuple sketch cannot express adopt's 7-key done-write, repair's phase+force-reason pair, migrate's phase+migrated_at pair, or bead 2's EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 marker-only writes), the SanctionedDerivedSync fence tightens to exactly-one with a one-assertion change and zero machinery rework, and all four flagged deviations A-D are justified. However, the fresh-read-under-lock contract does NOT fully close the TOCTOU class the spec pins: spec R3 (spec.md:113) requires the lock 'held across the read-stored -> derive -> guard-compare -> MergeMetadata critical section by repair phase', and its benign-residual claim rests on every serialized write being 'self-consistent at its write time'. repair.go computes detail.Derived at line 202, BEFORE lock acquisition, and only guard-compares under the lock. The stored side is genuinely fresh (phaselock.go:106, per-call NewCache), so AC-5(v)'s literal advancing-writer leg is closed (verified: TestRepairPhase_ConcurrentWriterNeverRegressed, repair_test.go:304). But the symmetric arm is open: when a concurrent writer lands a BACKWARD value — routine in bead 2, where every release of the sole claimed bead routes through SanctionedDerivedSync — repair's forward-stale pre-lock derivation passes IsBackwardMove(freshStored, staleDerived)=false and writes a value derived from a pre-lock children snapshot over the fresher sanctioned write, manufacturing the exact stored-vs-derived mismatch this spec exists to kill. The doc comment at repair.go:169-176 normalizes this ('deliberately exercises a STALE target') but it is an UNDECLARED deviation from the spec's pinned mechanism, absent from the A-D list, and the spec's own round-2 history rejects narrowed-window fixes by name. The fix is cheap now (SanctionedDerivedSync already models it: fresh-cache derive inside fn) and expensive if bead 2 discovers it. Everything else verified green: go build, internal/phase under -race, cmd/mindspec + internal/approve + internal/complete -short all pass; worktree left byte-identical; phase.lock ignored in both .gitignore:10 and gitutil.RuntimeIgnoreEntries.
concrete_changes_required: cmd/mindspec/repair.go: move the phase derivation inside WithPhaseWriteLock's critical section — call DerivePhaseDetail (or the children-read + DerivePhaseFromChildren pair, with a fresh per-call Cache, exactly as SanctionedDerivedSync does at sanctioned_sync.go:38-40) inside fn, so the guard compares fresh-stored against fresh-derived and the written value is self-consistent at write time per spec.md:113's pinned read-stored -> derive -> guard-compare -> MergeMetadata mechanism. Keep AC-5(v)'s stale-target concurrency leg by injecting the stale derivation through the existing test seams (SetListJSONForTest already controls the children the under-lock derive would see). fn's error return already aborts with no write, so the pre-lock DerivePhaseDetail error-path messaging moves into a captured-variable pattern like freshStored's.

internal/phase/phaselock.go: extend WithPhaseWriteLock's doc comment with the two caller obligations bead 2 needs stated to avoid repeating repair's pattern: (a) the freshness guarantee covers ONLY the stored mindspec_phase value passed to fn — every OTHER input to fn's decision (children sets, semantics markers, derived targets) must be read inside fn to be race-free; (b) the lock is non-reentrant — a caller already inside a critical section that calls WithPhaseWriteLock (e.g. wrapping SanctionedDerivedSync in an outer lock) self-blocks until the 10s ErrPhaseLockTimeout.

findings.title: Repair's derivation is computed pre-lock, leaving the backward-concurrent-writer arm of the TOCTOU open — an undeclared deviation from spec.md:113's pinned mechanism
findings.detail: Trace: repair.go:202 DerivePhaseDetail (pre-lock, snapshot children) -> repair.go:221 lock acquired, stored read fresh (phaselock.go:106) -> repair.go:223 IsBackwardMove(freshStored, STALE detail.Derived). Closed: concurrent ADVANCE (stale target ranks below fresh stored -> refuse; AC-5(v) test passes, final value review). Open: concurrent BACKWARD write (forced repair today; release's SanctionedDerivedSync routinely in bead 2) lands plan; repair's stale derived implement/review ranks forward -> writes a children-stale value over the fresher sanctioned write; final state disagrees with fresh children. Repair's write is then NOT 'self-consistent at its write time', contradicting the spec's benign-residual claim, and the spec's round-2 note ('re-derive-before-write only narrowed the window; this closes it') rejects exactly this narrowed-window shape. Not listed in deviations A-D despite repair.go:169-176 acknowledging the staleness.

findings.title: Deviation A: ENDORSED — the map-returning, epicID+seam-parameterized signature is the right long-term shape, and the plan's tuple sketch is unworkable
findings.detail: plan.md:531's WithPhaseWriteLock(root, fn func(stored) (write string, ok bool, err)) cannot express: adopt.go's 7-key done+audit map, repair's phase+mindspec_phase_force_reason pair, migrate's phase+mindspec_migrated_at pair, or bead 2's EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 'write the marker only, phase untouched' branch — so the divergence is necessity, not preference. epicID is required for the under-lock fresh read the plan itself demands. The mergeMetadata parameter preserves all six per-package fault-injection seams unchanged (plan/complete/impl/adopt/repair/migrate — verified passed through at every wrap site); hardcoding bead.MergeMetadata would have orphaned them. AC-5(vi) stays honest under this shape: the actual MergeMetadata invocation centralizes at phaselock.go:114, and writer_inventory_test.go's rule (any "mindspec_phase" composite literal must sit lexically inside a WithPhaseWriteLock CallExpr, resolved by import-path identity) turns red for a direct unlocked seam call AND for a literal built outside the lock call and passed by variable (conservatively unguarded). Residuals (const-key map, Sprintf-built JSON string, closure capturing the map for post-lock execution) are syntax-shaped and documented, matching the house adopt-fence's stated residual class. One future-proofing note: fn's nil-map-means-no-op vs non-nil-empty-map distinction is a Go footgun; all current callers return literals so it is dormant.

findings.title: Deviation B: ENDORSED — root parameter on EnsureMigrated/EnsureMigratedWithCache is the correct threading
findings.detail: The lock lives at <root>/.mindspec/phase.lock; internal/phase deriving root itself (findRoot) would invert layering. The three production call sites (plan.go:300, impl.go:277, complete.go:522) already hold root. Bonus for bead 2: EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 is planned for the same ahead-of-preflight sites, which now have root threaded. Note (benign, worth knowing): inside EnsureMigratedWithCache's fn the children read uses the SHARED caller cache c (migrate.go:72), so the derived backfill value can come from a pre-lock snapshot — acceptable only because the absent-check gate (stored != "" -> no-op) uses the fresh under-lock stored value, so a stale children derivation can only ever land when NO fresher stored value exists to clobber, and any concurrent locked writer serializes before (no-op) or after (overwrites). AC-5(vii)'s claim holds.

findings.title: Deviation C: ENDORSED — the arg2:unprovable registry entry's disclosed-residual rationale is honest
findings.detail: registries.go's new repairPhaseRunE arg2 entry mirrors the pre-existing arg1 entry's stated gap (specID/epicID interpolated into command-position Sprintfs without an own-arg idvalidate gate in this function), correctly notes both new recovery lines are idrender-rendered, and claims no new provenance class — which checks out: the multi-command refusal's operands (repair.go:250-251) are the same specID/epicID values arg1 already governs. Paired manifest line present. It registers rather than converts, pending the gate — the same honest posture as the sibling entry, not a rationale laundered to look closed.

findings.title: Deviation D: ENDORSED — anchor rewrite is forced by the wrap and the ordering assertions survive
findings.detail: The lock wrap replaces direct implPhaseMetadataFn(...) CallExprs with the seam passed as a bare-identifier argument to phase.WithPhaseWriteLock at impl.go:579/:618, so TestApproveImplCallOrder's AST anchors had to change shape or go permanently blind. internal/approve passes green including this test. Deep red-on-revert verification is R2's lane; from the contract side nothing about the new anchor shape constrains bead 2.

findings.title: Bead-2 fit: all five consumption points slot in without reshaping bead 1
findings.detail: (1) plan-approve value change: a one-literal edit inside the existing closure at plan.go:461. (2) next's first-claim advance: fn(stored) supports no-op-when-already-implement directly, and the writer-inventory test catches an unlocked variant by construction. (3) release -> SanctionedDerivedSync: swap the syncPhase deps closure (release.go:154) for the call; SanctionedDerivedSync already derives fresh-under-lock via its own NewCache (sanctioned_sync.go:38-40) — the model the repair fix in R3-1 should copy; its bare DerivePhaseFromChildren matches the spec's redesign leg, and the terminal-row limitation (all-closed -> review) is unreachable from release since the just-released bead is open by definition. (4) Fence tightening: change TestSanctionedDerivedSync_NoCallersOutsideAllowlist's final loop to len(sites)==1 && sites[0].file=="cmd/mindspec/release.go"; the collection machinery needs zero changes and the doc comment already carries the tightening instruction. (5) EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2: the closure shape supports marker+children reads inside fn and marker-only writes via the map return — but ONLY if the implementer knows the freshness guarantee stops at stored phase, hence the doc obligation in concrete change 2. Non-reentrancy is safe at all planned call sites (EnsureMigrated/EnsurePhaseSemanticsV2 run as sequential critical sections ahead of the verbs' own), but nesting SanctionedDerivedSync inside an outer lock would self-deadlock to timeout — worth the one doc line.
